budget_items.topic: Monty Tech FY27 total proposed budget
budget_items.what_was_said: The business manager presented Monty Tech's total FY27 proposed budget as a 2.53% increase. She said most of the increase was driven by required net school spending and transportation costs.

budget_items.topic: Monty Tech total assessment to all 18 communities
budget_items.what_was_said: The total FY27 assessment to all member communities was presented, described as a 6% increase over FY26.

budget_items.topic: Lunenburg's FY27 assessment to Monty Tech
budget_items.what_was_said: Lunenburg's proposed FY27 assessment to Monty Tech was presented as an increase driven almost entirely by the state's required minimum contribution formula.
The business manager walked through the chapter 70 formula, noting Monty Tech's foundation aid calculation produced only a small increase, so the state applied a hold-harmless $75-per-pupil minimum.

budget_items.topic: Monty Tech capital budget cut to offset athletic complex lease
budget_items.what_was_said: The business manager said Monty Tech cut its capital budget to offset the new operating cost of the athletic field/track and bleacher tax-exempt municipal lease.

budget_items.topic: Monty Tech budget cuts from initial request
budget_items.what_was_said: The business manager said Monty Tech had to cut its initial wish-list budget request by this amount to reach the proposed FY27 budget.

budget_items.topic: Monty Tech excess and deficiency (E&D) use
budget_items.what_was_said: Monty Tech's certified E&D (similar to free cash) was presented, with portions proposed to offset the operating and capital assessments to towns.

budget_items.topic: Storm water utility proposed FY27 budget
budget_items.what_was_said: The DPW presenter proposed a storm water utility budget to reach MS4 compliance, versus continuing to fund storm water only through the existing DPW operating line.

budget_items.topic: Storm water project manager position cost
budget_items.what_was_said: A new storm water project manager position was costed out including salary, fringe benefits, and a share of the DPW director's salary and benefits.
Vendor costs for engineering, catch basin cleaning and roadway sweeping were presented as the largest share of the proposed storm water utility budget.
The task force proposed a flat annual fee for single-family homes, citing comparable towns' fees as a benchmark.
Twenty-two capital projects were submitted for FY27 across departments, ranked by the capital planning committee.
The town manager said the preliminary capital plan is funded using a conservative free cash estimate, level taxation, and the special purpose stabilization fund, pending free cash certification.

budget_items.topic: Free cash history used to estimate FY27 capital funding
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager cited 10-year and 5-year free cash averages and medians as the basis for a conservative FY27 free cash estimate.
The town manager described the special purpose stabilization fund, created in 2017 for vehicles/equipment, noting its current balance and that it has never been used.
The town manager reported the town is deficit-spending on snow and ice, already well over budget with much of winter remaining, which affects free cash available for other uses.
The town manager said TC Pacios building carries unbudgeted annual operating costs and that decommissioning half the building produced far less utility savings than expected.
The town manager flagged the FY27 mosquito control program assessment as a possible town meeting article given the town's financial condition.
The town manager reported a grant application for design funding for the Goodrich Street culvert.
The town manager reported a grant application for network infrastructure upgrades at the Adult Activity Center, a project unlikely to be funded within the FY27 capital plan itself.

decisions.decision: An additional capital planning committee meeting was scheduled for the following Wednesday to discuss initial reactions to the preliminary FY27 capital plan.

The chair asked department heads to include in their FY27 budget presentations: a summary of key services, a status-quo vs. proposed-changes summary, funding sources outside taxation, and an organizational chart.
A committee member agreed to collect finance committee members' detailed budget questions for each department and forward them to the town manager/finance director in advance of presentations.
The public schools budget presentation to the Finance Committee was set for February 19.
Warrant articles for the May 2 annual town meeting are due by March 16.
The town manager will begin meeting with TC Pacios building stakeholders (including cable access and the food pantry) starting the next day about winding down operations there.

minutes.summary: The Finance Committee opened FY27 budget season by hearing Monty Tech's proposed budget, whose per-town assessment formula would raise Lunenburg's cost significantly more than Monty Tech's own budget grew; then heard a storm water task force pitch to create a dedicated storm water utility, which several committee members criticized as inefficient compared to funding it through the regular operating budget; and closed with a preliminary, free-cash-dependent FY27 capital plan and a town manager's report describing ongoing finance department turnover, an unclosed FY25 books, and a likely need for an override or cuts in FY27. No budget or override decisions were made; this was described as an early, non-binding discussion.

what_happened.line: The town manager said an override or cuts are likely for FY27, citing budget pressure across departments.
Lunenburg's FY27 assessment to Monty Tech would rise mainly because of the state's minimum contribution formula, not Monty Tech's own spending growth.
A storm water task force proposed a dedicated utility funded by a flat homeowner fee; several committee members argued the operating budget would be more efficient.
The finance department reported ongoing staff turnover and FY25 books still not closed, complicating FY27 budget preparation.
A preliminary FY27 capital plan listing ranked projects across departments was presented, pending free cash certification.

why_it_matters: An override, if it goes to a town-wide vote, would raise property tax bills beyond the normal cap and residents would decide it directly.
A separate storm water utility, if adopted, would likely show up as a new fee on homeowners rather than as part of the existing tax-funded budget.
Monty Tech's assessment increase and Lunenburg's own department budgets both feed the same FY27 town budget that goes to the May 2 annual town meeting.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records overlap heavily on the Monty Tech and storm-water dollar figures and on several capital/snow-ice figures (mostly matching once caption garbling is corrected), but each omits substantial material the other has: our minutes skip the entire Town Manager/Finance Director report section (new Finance Director, free cash certification, payroll transition) and several capital-plan and Monty Tech figures the official minutes give, while the official minutes omit most of the granular dollar figures we captured from the recording (E&D use, chapter 70 aid, capital funding sources, stabilization fund) and several decisions we recorded. The single most important thing to check is the conflicting figure for Lunenburg's Monty Tech assessment ($1,452,379 heard vs. $1,378,183 in the official minutes) and the TC Pacios/Passios building status, which read as two different levels of decisiveness.
